chunks: Al-‘Abbās narrated from Al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī, from Aḥmad ibn ‘Umar, from Marwān ibn Muslim, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: My brother is in Baghdad, and I fear that he may die there.
He said: “It does not matter to you wherever he dies. Indeed, no one remains in the east of the earth nor in its west except that Allah gathers his soul to Wādī al-Salām.”
He said: I said: May I be made your ransom, “And where is Wādī al-Salām?”
He said: “It is at the back of al-Kūfah. Indeed, it is as though I see them in circles, sitting and conversing.”

key_terms.بِبَغْدَادَ: in Baghdad, the place mentioned by the questioner regarding his brother
key_terms.حَشَرَ: gathered, meaning Allah brings together the soul after death
key_terms.حَلَقًا: circles or rings, describing their grouped arrangement
key_terms.رُوحَهُ: his soul, referring to the human soul after death
key_terms.ظَهْرُ الْكُوفَةِ: the back of al-Kūfah, identified as the location of Wādī al-Salām
key_terms.وَادِي السَّلَامِ: Wādī al-Salām, the place to which souls are gathered
key_terms.يَتَحَدَّثُونَ: speaking with one another, describing their interaction

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about Wādī al-Salām and where souls are gathered after death?
ai.summary: This hadith describes that the place of a believer’s death does not prevent the soul from being gathered by Allah to Wādī al-Salām. It identifies Wādī al-Salām as being behind al-Kūfah and portrays the souls there as assembled in circles, sitting and speaking, indicating a posthumous state of gathering.
